newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek seamen renew strike, rubbish strike ends.
newsitem.headline: Greek seamen renew strike, rubbish strike ends.

text.p: Ships remained at port in Greece on Monday after seamen renewed their strike for better benefits but Athens rubbish collectors suspended a week-long walkout after extensive floods hit the country.
The Panhellenic Seamen's Federation (PNO) renewed a strike suspended after five days in late December to press for better benefits for unemployment, pensions, insurance and tax.
Monday was the first day of the 48-hour walkout and PNO will meet on Tuesday to decide whether to extend the strike if their demands are not met, union spokesman Christos Katagas said.
Seamen went on strike before Christmas but suspended the action for the holidays after causing extensive disruptions.
"Our original decision, if nothing changes, is for the strike to continue," Katagas told Reuters.

The weather service warned passenger ships on Monday against leaving port in bad weather, making an assessment of the effect of the strike difficult but Piraeus port authority officials said the seamen's strike was affecting sailings out of Greece's main port.
Athens rubbish collectors called off a week-long srike on Monday, after heavy floods swept tonnes of garbage on to the capital's streets,
Five people have been killed and one is still missing, while towns and villages have been choked with masses of muddy rubble after the waters receded on Monday.
Rubbish collectors suspended their strike until February 20, as a goodwill gesture to Athenians and because of health hazards.
Union representatives said Interior Minister Alekos Papadopoulos had promised to satisfy their main demand, the conversion of temporary contracts into permanent ones.
